name: Marginal Man
label: Dischord
lede: Marginal Man ran two guitars when DC hardcore mostly ran one, took its name from a sociology class, and said goodbye with two sold-out sets at the 9:30 Club, the room where it had started.

eras.title: Outside looking in
eras.text: Artificial Peace had just folded, and three of its members wanted something bigger and more tuneful. They added Kenny Inouye, a kid who went to every one of their shows, on second guitar, and walked onstage at the 9:30 Club as one of DC's first twin-guitar hardcore bands.

years.h: Three Artificial Peace veterans go looking for a second guitarist
years.p: Singer [[Steve Polcari|33611a9d-0a07-418b-ac27-b51a58f93561]], guitarist [[Pete Murray|6ab4a566-a279-441a-af5f-4d47459e1c18]] and drummer [[Mike Manos|2da8a8ac-dab6-4b39-9ca6-ce91fee93fcf]] add [[Kenny Inouye|a2ae807d-953b-496b-ac75-62d55c5f0afc]] on second guitar and [[Andre Lee|b9484df3-7dce-4c9b-be55-072f26ca9498]] on bass. Inouye says he got on their radar by showing up to their shows.

years.h: Kenny Inouye lifts the band's name from a sociology class
years.p: Marginal Man is his idea: a person partly assimilated into two or more cultures but fully into none.
years.xp: Steve Polcari has explained it the same way from the scene side: friends in two or more groups, belonging to none. For a band of Bethesda and DC kids caught between hardcore's first wave and whatever came next, it fit.

years.cap: Flier for the 9:30 Club show, January 2, 1983, with Faith and Minor Threat
years.h: Marginal Man debut at the 9:30 Club, and the room sells out twice
years.p: Dischord dates the band's debut for DC crowds to the "555" concert. Kenny Inouye remembers their first real show as two sold-out sets opening for [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]].
years.xp:
Inouye told This Is Albatross people came from New Jersey, New York and Boston, which is why the club ran two sets. Wikipedia lists an earlier warm-up, a basement show on November 19, 1982, with [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], Insurrection, Double-O and [[United Mutation|40d5b767-7978-4956-8245-586c1dd0b01d]]. The 9:30 Club was the real introduction, per Dischord.

Two guitars set them apart. Most DC hardcore bands of 1981 and 1982 ran on one, and Marginal Man's layered sound pointed toward the more melodic records the city would make a few years later.

eras.title: One Dischord record, then the road
eras.text: Identity was Marginal Man's one Dischord record. When a second didn't come together, the band took Double Image to Gasatanka/Enigma and spent the mid-80s touring the country harder than most of DC.

years.cap: Flier for the Wilson Center show, October 13, 1984, with Meatmen, United Mutation and Beefeater
years.h: Identity is Dischord No. 13, cut at Inner Ear
years.p: Marginal Man's only Dischord record, a 12" EP. The cover art is by Manolo Lagdameo, the band's roadie.

years.big: "We were the first band on Dischord to put out a record on a label other than Dischord."
q: We didn't get a no, but we also didn't get a yes.
years.h: Marginal Man leave Dischord for Gasatanka/Enigma and Double Image
years.p: Kenny Inouye on the follow-up to Identity, which came out on Gasatanka/Enigma instead.
years.xp:
Inouye has told it without bitterness: Dischord was in a shaky financial spot, and the band wanted the record out on time, so they looked elsewhere. He says [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] never objected.

[[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] of Minor Threat helped shape Double Image, mostly by telling them what wasn't working. Etched in the inner groove: "70% of 0 is Pizza", a souvenir of a Denver show where the promoter paid them in pizza instead of door money.

yt: Live at Lake Braddock Community Center, December 20, 1985
years.p: Marginal Man's first full-length came out on Gasatanka/Enigma in 1985. In Your Eye reissued it, distributed by Dischord.

years.h: A WGNS compilation of the new DC wave picks up Marginal Man
Marginal Man tour the country on a DIY budget
years.p: Early tours ran with roadie Manolo Lagdameo along. The band shared bills with the Circle Jerks, TSOL, [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] and Corrosion of Conformity.
years.xp: Kenny Inouye says Necros and COC looked out for younger bands. He remembers the second tour as 31 or 32 dates in 35 days, with Death Piggy (Dave Brockie's band before GWAR), Corrosion of Conformity and the Big Boys along the way.

years.h: Full set at GWU's Marvin Center, 1985
yt: Full set at GWU's Marvin Center, 1985

eras.title: Going out on a high note
eras.text: By the late 80s the members were writing in different directions, and the self-titled last LP showed it. Rather than drift into being a legacy act, they booked two farewell shows at the 9:30 Club.

years.h: The self-titled last LP lands on Giant Records
years.p: A transitional record, with each writer pulling his own way. Kenny Inouye still counts some of his favorite songs on it.

years.cap: Flier for the farewell, 9:30 Club, March 24, 1988, with Shudder to Think
years.h: Marginal Man go out with two sold-out sets at the 9:30
years.p: The band headlines the club where it debuted, with [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] opening both sets. Kenny Inouye says the choice was fade away or go out on a high note.
years.xp: After the farewell, Inouye applied for the booking job at the 9:30 Club and got it. He told This Is Albatross he booked local bands there for about two and a half years, at what he called his favorite club.

eras.title: Back for single nights, and a booking desk
eras.text: Marginal Man kept coming back for one night at a time. Kenny Inouye ended up booking the 9:30 Club, where the band had started, and Dischord kept Identity in print on CD.

years.h: Dischord's State of the Union compilation includes Marginal Man
years.p: A Marginal Man track on Dischord No. 32, released in 1989.
Marginal Man play the first of several single shows after the 1988 farewell.

years.h: Another one-night Marginal Man show closes out 1995
years.p: Marginal Man play again on December 30.
Dischord reissues Marginal Man's 1984 EP on CD.

eras.title: One more at the Black Cat
eras.text: Twenty-three years after the farewell, all five members played again, this time at the Black Cat, the club run by fellow DC veteran Dante Ferrando.

years.h: Twenty-three years on, Marginal Man play the Black Cat
years.p: The Washington Post previewed the reunion as tracks from a formative period. Kenny Inouye had by then booked the 9:30 Club himself; he now works at the University of Hawaiʻi–West Oʻahu.
years.xp: Inouye's father was Senator Daniel Inouye, who came to several of Marginal Man's early shows.
